question.text: Who needs a Nevada license to drive, and who are the stated exceptions?

answer.text: Anyone who lives or works in Nevada and wants to drive on its streets and highways needs a Nevada license; employees from border states and military members stationed in Nevada are the stated exceptions.

teaching.text: If you live or work here and drive here, you need the Nevada card; only border-state employees and military members stationed in Nevada are named as exceptions. Remember: live or work here, license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Anyone who lives or works in Nevada and wants to drive on its streets and highways needs a Nevada license; employees from border states and military members stationed in Nevada are the stated exceptions.

question.text: How long does a new Nevada resident have to apply for a Nevada driver license?

answer.text: Someone who moves to Nevada from another state has thirty days after becoming a resident to apply for a Nevada driver license.

teaching.text: The thirty days start when you become a resident, so the switch from an old state's license is expected within your first month. Remember: thirty days to switch.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Someone who moves to Nevada from another state has thirty days after becoming a resident to apply for a Nevada driver license.

question.text: What steps and proofs does a Nevada license applicant need, and what is the minimum age?

answer.text: An applicant fills out an application, visits a full-service DMV office, must be at least sixteen years old, and proves full legal name, age, Nevada residency and a Social Security Number if one was ever issued.

teaching.text: Think of four proofs plus an office visit: legal name, age, Nevada residency and any Social Security Number, at sixteen or older. Remember: sixteen, four proofs, office visit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An applicant fills out an application, visits a full-service DMV office, must be at least sixteen years old, and proves full legal name, age, Nevada residency and a Social Security Number if one was ever issued.

question.text: Do you need a Social Security Number to get a Driver Authorization Card?

answer.text: A Social Security Number is not needed to get a Driver Authorization Card (DAC).

teaching.text: The Driver Authorization Card is the one credential in this chapter that asks for no Social Security Number at all. Remember: DAC needs no SSN.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Social Security Number is not needed to get a Driver Authorization Card (DAC).

question.text: How long is a first Nevada license valid for someone under sixty-five, and when does it expire?

answer.text: A first-time license issued to someone under age sixty-five lasts eight years and expires on the holder's birthday.

teaching.text: Eight years is the first-license term for anyone under sixty-five, and it always ends on the birthday. Remember: eight years, birthday ends.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A first-time license issued to someone under age sixty-five lasts eight years and expires on the holder's birthday.

question.text: When does a license expire if limited-term immigration documents proved name and birth date?

answer.text: If limited-term immigration documents were used as proof of name and birth date, the license expires on the departure date verified electronically by DHS, or after one year when DHS supplies no date.

teaching.text: Limited-term immigration papers tie the license to the departure date DHS verifies, with one year as the fallback. Remember: departure date or one year.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If limited-term immigration documents were used as proof of name and birth date, the license expires on the departure date verified electronically by DHS, or after one year when DHS supplies no date.

question.text: What is the longest any Nevada license or identification card can be valid?

answer.text: Under NRS four hundred eighty-three point two nine zero a Nevada driver license or identification card can never be valid for longer than eight years.

teaching.text: State law sets the ceiling: no Nevada license or ID card ever runs past eight years. Remember: never beyond eight years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under NRS four hundred eighty-three point two nine zero a Nevada driver license or identification card can never be valid for longer than eight years.

question.text: How long are licenses valid for drivers sixty-five and older, compared with ID cards?

answer.text: Licenses for drivers aged sixty-five and older are valid for four years, while identification cards are valid for eight years.

teaching.text: At sixty-five the license term drops to four years, but an identification card keeps its eight-year term. Remember: sixty-five plus means four.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Licenses for drivers aged sixty-five and older are valid for four years, while identification cards are valid for eight years.

question.text: Who must co-sign for an applicant under eighteen, and what does that co-signer accept?

answer.text: An applicant under eighteen needs a co-signer (a custodial parent, a legal guardian or another person allowed by NRS four hundred eighty-three point three zero zero), and that co-signer shares liability for damage the minor causes by negligent or willful driving.

teaching.text: The co-signer is not just a signature; that person shares liability for damage the young driver causes. Remember: co-signer shares the liability.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An applicant under eighteen needs a co-signer (a custodial parent, a legal guardian or another person allowed by NRS four hundred eighty-three point three zero zero), and that co-signer shares liability for damage the minor causes by negligent or willful driving.

question.text: How do the license terms by age compare with the ID card term?

answer.text: A first license for someone under sixty-five runs eight years, a license for someone sixty-five or older runs four years, and an identification card runs eight years.

teaching.text: Line the three up: under sixty-five gets eight, sixty-five and older gets four, and the ID card stays at eight. Remember: eight, four, ID eight.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A first license for someone under sixty-five runs eight years, a license for someone sixty-five or older runs four years, and an identification card runs eight years.

question.text: How does the Social Security rule differ for a license and a Driver Authorization Card?

answer.text: A driver license applicant must prove a Social Security Number if one was issued, but a Driver Authorization Card applicant needs no Social Security Number at all.

teaching.text: The Social Security rule splits the two credentials: license applicants prove the number if one exists, DAC applicants never do. Remember: license yes, DAC no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver license applicant must prove a Social Security Number if one was issued, but a Driver Authorization Card applicant needs no Social Security Number at all.

question.text: How many licenses or ID cards may a Nevada resident hold, and what happens to an out-of-state card?

answer.text: A Nevada resident may hold only one driver license or ID card, so a card from another state, US territory or foreign country must be surrendered; it is voided and handed back.

teaching.text: One person, one active card: an out-of-state card is voided and handed back when the Nevada card is issued. Remember: one card, surrender others.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Nevada resident may hold only one driver license or ID card, so a card from another state, US territory or foreign country must be surrendered; it is voided and handed back.

question.text: Which test does a new resident always take, and when can the others be waived?

answer.text: A new resident always takes the vision test, and the other tests can be waived only when every one of the listed transfer conditions is met.

teaching.text: Vision is the test no newcomer skips; knowledge and road tests drop away only when the whole checklist is met. Remember: vision always, others maybe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A new resident always takes the vision test, and the other tests can be waived only when every one of the listed transfer conditions is met.

question.text: What driving-record condition must a new resident meet for a test waiver?

answer.text: Waiver condition: fewer than three moving violations in the past four years, and no suspension, revocation or cancellation of the license.

teaching.text: The record test has two parts: fewer than three moving violations in four years, and no suspension, revocation or cancellation. Remember: under three in four.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Waiver condition: fewer than three moving violations in the past four years, and no suspension, revocation or cancellation of the license.

question.text: What DUI condition applies to a new resident's test waiver?

answer.text: Waiver condition: no DUI conviction within the past seven years.

teaching.text: The DUI look-back is longer than the violation window: seven years with no DUI conviction. Remember: no DUI in seven.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Waiver condition: no DUI conviction within the past seven years.

question.text: What restriction, license and age conditions complete the waiver list?

answer.text: Waiver conditions: no restriction on the driving privilege that calls for an evaluation, a valid out-of-state license of the same class being applied for, and an age of twenty-one or older.

teaching.text: Three more boxes to tick: no restriction calling for an evaluation, a valid same-class license, and age twenty-one or older. Remember: same class, twenty-one plus.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Waiver conditions: no restriction on the driving privilege that calls for an evaluation, a valid out-of-state license of the same class being applied for, and an age of twenty-one or older.

question.text: Does an active-duty service member with a valid home-state license need a Nevada license?

answer.text: An active-duty member of the US Armed Forces who holds a valid home-state license does not need a Nevada license.

teaching.text: An active-duty service member keeps driving on a valid home-state license with no Nevada license needed. Remember: duty license still works.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An active-duty member of the US Armed Forces who holds a valid home-state license does not need a Nevada license.

question.text: When may out-of-state students, tourists and seasonal residents drive without a Nevada license?

answer.text: Non-residents such as out-of-state students, tourists and seasonal residents may drive in Nevada without a Nevada license if they are at least sixteen, hold a valid home-state license and obey Nevada traffic and financial responsibility laws.

teaching.text: Students, tourists and seasonal residents can drive on a home license if they are sixteen, licensed at home and follow Nevada's laws. Remember: visitors: sixteen, valid, lawful.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Non-residents such as out-of-state students, tourists and seasonal residents may drive in Nevada without a Nevada license if they are at least sixteen, hold a valid home-state license and obey Nevada traffic and financial responsibility laws.

question.text: Which national databases check every driver record, and what does a problem elsewhere block?

answer.text: Every driver record is run through two national databases, the Problem Driver Pointer System and the CDL Information System, and a privilege suspended, revoked, canceled or denied elsewhere blocks a Nevada license until that issue is cleared, though an ID card may still be possible meanwhile.

teaching.text: Two national databases follow a driver's record, so a suspension elsewhere must be cleared before a Nevada license is possible. Remember: two databases, record follows.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every driver record is run through two national databases, the Problem Driver Pointer System and the CDL Information System, and a privilege suspended, revoked, canceled or denied elsewhere blocks a Nevada license until that issue is cleared, though an ID card may still be possible meanwhile.

question.text: Which new-resident test is never waived, and which ones can be?

answer.text: The vision test is always given to a new resident, while the knowledge and road tests may be waived only when all of the transfer conditions hold.

teaching.text: Every waiver still leaves the vision test in place; only the knowledge and road tests can be set aside. Remember: vision never waived.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The vision test is always given to a new resident, while the knowledge and road tests may be waived only when all of the transfer conditions hold.

question.text: How do the rules differ for an active-duty member and for other non-residents?

answer.text: An active-duty service member needs only a valid home-state license, while a non-resident student, tourist or seasonal resident must also be at least sixteen and follow Nevada traffic and financial responsibility laws.

teaching.text: The service member needs only the home license, while other visitors also need the age and the law-abiding conditions. Remember: military simpler than visitors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An active-duty service member needs only a valid home-state license, while a non-resident student, tourist or seasonal resident must also be at least sixteen and follow Nevada traffic and financial responsibility laws.

question.text: What kind of document proves full legal name and date of birth, with examples?

answer.text: Proof of full legal name and date of birth is one unexpired original or certified document, for example a state-issued birth certificate, a valid US passport or passport card, a Consular Report of Birth Abroad (FS-two hundred forty), or another state's license, permit or ID bearing a DHS-approved Real ID mark.

teaching.text: The key words are one, unexpired, and original or certified, such as a state birth certificate or a valid passport. Remember: one original, unexpired document.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Proof of full legal name and date of birth is one unexpired original or certified document, for example a state-issued birth certificate, a valid US passport or passport card, a Consular Report of Birth Abroad (FS-two hundred forty), or another state's license, permit or ID bearing a DHS-approved Real ID mark.

question.text: Can a Nevada Department of Corrections ID card prove name and birth date?

answer.text: A Nevada Department of Corrections ID card can prove name and birth date, but not for a Real ID.

teaching.text: A corrections ID card helps with a standard card, but it stops at the Real ID door. Remember: corrections card, not Real ID.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Nevada Department of Corrections ID card can prove name and birth date, but not for a Real ID.

question.text: Does an out-of-state Real ID marked limited term prove name and birth date?

answer.text: An out-of-state Real ID marked limited term does not prove name and birth date; acceptable immigration documents have to be shown instead.

teaching.text: A Real ID from another state marked limited term is not enough, so the applicant brings acceptable immigration documents instead. Remember: limited term won't prove.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An out-of-state Real ID marked limited term does not prove name and birth date; acceptable immigration documents have to be shown instead.

question.text: Which documents do not prove name and age?

answer.text: These do not prove name and age: a hospital-issued birth certificate, a license or ID from another US state, territory or foreign country, a foreign birth certificate, a Border Crossing Card or a Consular Identification Card.

teaching.text: Watch the source of the document: hospital and foreign birth certificates, Border Crossing Cards and Consular ID cards are all refused. Remember: hospital certificate does not count.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: These do not prove name and age: a hospital-issued birth certificate, a license or ID from another US state, territory or foreign country, a foreign birth certificate, a Border Crossing Card or a Consular Identification Card.

question.text: What must you bring when your current name differs from your identity document?

answer.text: When your current name differs from your identity document, bring legal proof of the change such as a marriage certificate, a divorce decree that mentions the name change, a spouse's death certificate, an adoption record or a court order, as an original or certified copy.

teaching.text: Bridge the gap between names with legal proof, such as a marriage certificate, a divorce decree, an adoption record or a court order. Remember: name changed, bring proof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When your current name differs from your identity document, bring legal proof of the change such as a marriage certificate, a divorce decree that mentions the name change, a spouse's death certificate, an adoption record or a court order, as an original or certified copy.

question.text: How do a corrections ID card and an out-of-state limited-term Real ID differ as proof?

answer.text: A Nevada Department of Corrections ID card proves name and birth date for a standard card but not for Real ID, while another state's limited-term Real ID proves neither.

teaching.text: The corrections card is accepted with a limit, while the limited-term out-of-state Real ID is refused outright. Remember: limits versus refused.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Nevada Department of Corrections ID card proves name and birth date for a standard card but not for Real ID, while another state's limited-term Real ID proves neither.

question.text: Which version of the Resident Alien Card is accepted, and which is refused?

answer.text: An old Resident Alien Card printed with no expiration date is accepted as a Permanent Resident Card; any other version of the Resident Alien Card is refused as proof of name, birth date or lawful status.

teaching.text: Only the old Resident Alien Card with no expiration date passes; every other version is refused. Remember: undated card only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An old Resident Alien Card printed with no expiration date is accepted as a Permanent Resident Card; any other version of the Resident Alien Card is refused as proof of name, birth date or lawful status.

question.text: Must holders of the undated Resident Alien Card replace it?

answer.text: The DMV will not force holders of the undated card to replace it unless DHS requests it, and the card rules may change with Department of Homeland Security policy.

teaching.text: Holders of the undated card keep it unless DHS asks for a replacement, and the rule can change with federal policy. Remember: replace only if requested.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The DMV will not force holders of the undated card to replace it unless DHS requests it, and the card rules may change with Department of Homeland Security policy.

question.text: What must accompany an expired I-ninety-four?

answer.text: An expired I-ninety-four, whether with a permanent-resident passport stamp or with a US visa, must be paired with a Notice of Action (I-seven hundred ninety-seven) that shows an approved extension.

teaching.text: An expired I-ninety-four never stands alone; it needs a Notice of Action showing an approved extension. Remember: expired needs approved extension.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An expired I-ninety-four, whether with a permanent-resident passport stamp or with a US visa, must be paired with a Notice of Action (I-seven hundred ninety-seven) that shows an approved extension.

question.text: What card do limited-term documents produce, and how is lawful status checked?

answer.text: Limited-term documents such as an Employment Authorization Card (I-seven hundred sixty-six) produce a card marked Limited Term, and every immigration document is electronically checked for lawful status.

teaching.text: Limited-term papers lead to a card marked Limited Term, and every immigration document is checked electronically. Remember: limited documents, limited card.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Limited-term documents such as an Employment Authorization Card (I-seven hundred sixty-six) produce a card marked Limited Term, and every immigration document is electronically checked for lawful status.

question.text: Which documents prove a Social Security Number, and which paystubs are refused?

answer.text: Proof of Social Security Number is a Social Security card, a W-two or IRS Form one thousand ninety-nine showing the full number, or a paystub with full legal name; handwritten paystubs are refused and every document must be an original showing the complete number.

teaching.text: Social Security proof must show the whole number on an original, and a handwritten paystub is never accepted. Remember: full number, original only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Proof of Social Security Number is a Social Security card, a W-two or IRS Form one thousand ninety-nine showing the full number, or a paystub with full legal name; handwritten paystubs are refused and every document must be an original showing the complete number.

question.text: What do alternative documents for name, age and Social Security require?

answer.text: Alternative documents for name, age and Social Security Number need supervisory approval and can never be used to issue a Real ID card.

teaching.text: Alternative documents open the door only with a supervisor's approval, and never for a Real ID card. Remember: supervisor yes, Real ID no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alternative documents for name, age and Social Security Number need supervisory approval and can never be used to issue a Real ID card.

question.text: What must a translated document include?

answer.text: Translated documents must cover the entire original, be typed or printed electronically, and carry a signed statement in which the translator certifies the translation is complete and accurate and that they are fluent in both languages.

teaching.text: A translation must be complete and typed or printed, with the translator signing that it is accurate and that they are fluent in both languages. Remember: whole, typed, certified translation.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Translated documents must cover the entire original, be typed or printed electronically, and carry a signed statement in which the translator certifies the translation is complete and accurate and that they are fluent in both languages.

question.text: How can you tell a Real ID card from a standard card?

answer.text: A Real ID license or ID shows a gold Nevada outline with a star cutout, while a standard card carries the words NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES.

teaching.text: Look for the gold Nevada outline with the star; the standard card instead says it is not for Real ID purposes. Remember: gold star means Real.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Real ID license or ID shows a gold Nevada outline with a star cutout, while a standard card carries the words NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES.

question.text: What choice do Nevada applicants have, and what must the DMV verify?

answer.text: Nevada applicants may choose either a Real ID compliant card or a standard card, and the DMV must verify identity, birth date, Social Security Number, lawful status and primary residential address.

teaching.text: Every applicant picks Real ID or standard, and either way the DMV verifies identity, birth date, Social Security, lawful status and address. Remember: choose Real or standard.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Nevada applicants may choose either a Real ID compliant card or a standard card, and the DMV must verify identity, birth date, Social Security Number, lawful status and primary residential address.

question.text: How many residency documents does a Real ID applicant present, and what must they show?

answer.text: A Real ID applicant presents two documents proving Nevada residency that show the correct residential address, such as utility bills, mortgage statements, rental agreements or bank statements.

teaching.text: A Real ID applicant brings two address documents, such as utility bills, mortgage statements, rental agreements or bank statements. Remember: two papers, right address.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Real ID applicant presents two documents proving Nevada residency that show the correct residential address, such as utility bills, mortgage statements, rental agreements or bank statements.

question.text: How does a Real ID card differ from a standard card in markings and standards?

answer.text: A Real ID card has the gold Nevada outline and star cutout and meets federal standards, while a standard card says NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES and does not.

teaching.text: The star card meets federal standards; the card printed NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES does not. Remember: star federal, standard not.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Real ID card has the gold Nevada outline and star cutout and meets federal standards, while a standard card says NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES and does not.

question.text: Can alternative identity documents support a Real ID card?

answer.text: Alternative identity documents can support a standard card with supervisory approval but are never accepted for a Real ID card.

teaching.text: Alternative documents can support a standard card with approval, but a Real ID card always needs the regular evidence. Remember: alternatives never for Real.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alternative identity documents can support a standard card with supervisory approval but are never accepted for a Real ID card.

question.text: What is the purpose of the Real ID Act?

answer.text: The Real ID Act of May two thousand five aims to fight terrorism, identity theft and other crimes by tightening the security of state-issued identification.

teaching.text: The Real ID Act aimed to fight terrorism, identity theft and other crimes by making state cards harder to fake. Remember: tighter IDs fight crime.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Real ID Act of May two thousand five aims to fight terrorism, identity theft and other crimes by tightening the security of state-issued identification.

question.text: What must a standard license holder show to upgrade to Real ID?

answer.text: A standard Nevada license holder who upgrades to Real ID must again show documents for name, birth date, Social Security Number and Nevada residential address, and they may be scanned, stored and electronically verified.

teaching.text: Upgrading from standard to Real ID means bringing every document again, and the DMV may scan and verify them. Remember: upgrade means documents again.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A standard Nevada license holder who upgrades to Real ID must again show documents for name, birth date, Social Security Number and Nevada residential address, and they may be scanned, stored and electronically verified.

question.text: How long is a Driver Authorization Card valid, and how are renewals handled?

answer.text: A Driver Authorization Card is valid for four years, expires on the holder's birthday and must be carried whenever the holder drives; renewals and address changes are done in person only.

teaching.text: The DAC runs four years, ends on the birthday, rides along whenever you drive, and is renewed in person. Remember: four years, in person.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Driver Authorization Card is valid for four years, expires on the holder's birthday and must be carried whenever the holder drives; renewals and address changes are done in person only.

question.text: Which single document can support a DAC application?

answer.text: For a DAC you may show one document from the main identity list, or one of a US military ID, a US military dependent ID, a US Armed Forces discharge document or a US Certificate of Degree of Indian Blood.

teaching.text: One document is enough for a DAC when it comes from the main identity list or the short military and tribal list. Remember: one main or military document.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a DAC you may show one document from the main identity list, or one of a US military ID, a US military dependent ID, a US Armed Forces discharge document or a US Certificate of Degree of Indian Blood.

question.text: Which second-list documents can a DAC applicant show instead, and how many?

answer.text: A DAC applicant may instead show two documents from a second list: a license, ID or DAC from another state, DC or a US territory, a foreign passport, a foreign birth certificate, a Mexican Federal Electoral Card, a Consular Identification Card or a similar foreign-government document.

question.text: What can a Driver Authorization Card not be used for?

answer.text: A DAC is not valid for federal or state identification and cannot establish eligibility for Nevada benefits, licenses or services, and DAC application information is not used to decide legal presence or immigration status.

teaching.text: A DAC is a driving card only; it never works as identification or as proof for Nevada benefits. Remember: drive only, not identify.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A DAC is not valid for federal or state identification and cannot establish eligibility for Nevada benefits, licenses or services, and DAC application information is not used to decide legal presence or immigration status.

question.text: How does a Driver Authorization Card compare with a license and with identification?

answer.text: A Driver Authorization Card works like a license for driving and follows the same rules unless the handbook says otherwise, yet it cannot serve as identification for any federal or state purpose.

teaching.text: The DAC follows the license rules on the road, yet it can never serve as identification for any government purpose. Remember: drives yes, identifies no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Driver Authorization Card works like a license for driving and follows the same rules unless the handbook says otherwise, yet it cannot serve as identification for any federal or state purpose.

question.text: Who must prove a Nevada residential address?

answer.text: Applicants for an original Real ID or standard ID card, instruction permit or driver license must prove a Nevada residential address, and DAC applicants must do so at original issuance.

teaching.text: Every original card or permit needs Nevada address proof, and DAC applicants give it at original issuance. Remember: new cards need address proof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants for an original Real ID or standard ID card, instruction permit or driver license must prove a Nevada residential address, and DAC applicants must do so at original issuance.

question.text: How many residency documents are needed, and how recent must they be?

answer.text: Residency is proven with originals or certified copies of any two listed documents showing a Nevada residential address; one group of documents must be dated within sixty days, the other group may be the last one issued.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Residency is proven with originals or certified copies of any two listed documents showing a Nevada residential address; one group of documents must be dated within sixty days, the other group may be the last one issued.

question.text: When does a hotel, motel, RV park or campground record count as residency proof?

answer.text: A hotel, motel, RV park or campground record counts as residency proof only if it shows at least thirty consecutive days of living in Nevada.

question.text: How can a parent or guardian prove the residence of an applicant under eighteen?

answer.text: For an applicant under eighteen, a parent or guardian can prove the applicant's residence with two listed documents or by signing a DMV-approved form confirming they share the same address.

question.text: Which three department-approved forms can prove residency?

answer.text: The three department-approved residency forms are the Relief Agency or Shelter Certification (DMV one hundred fifteen), the Property Owner Residency Affidavit (DMV one hundred sixteen) and the Certification of Nevada Residency (DMV five).

question.text: Which home-owner and voter documents count as residency proof?

teaching.text: A notarized statement from the home owner and a voter registration card are both on the residency list. Remember: notarized owner, voter card.

question.text: What happens if you need glasses or contact lenses to pass the vision standard?

answer.text: If you need glasses or contact lenses to meet the vision standard, a restriction is placed on your license.

teaching.text: Needing glasses or contacts to pass vision does not stop you; it adds a restriction to the license. Remember: lenses needed, restriction added.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you need glasses or contact lenses to meet the vision standard, a restriction is placed on your license.

question.text: What does the knowledge test check, and how can it be taken?

question.text: What do the initial tests and each retest cost?

answer.text: Initial knowledge and skills tests carry a twenty-five dollars fee, and each retest needed before the license is issued costs ten dollars.

question.text: What does the examiner check on your vehicle before the road test?

answer.text: Before the road test the examiner checks the registration and plates, proof of insurance, headlights, taillights, brake lights, turn signals, horn, seat belts, tires and windshield wipers.

question.text: What must the road-test vehicle have, and who may ride along?

answer.text: The test vehicle must be safe with working brakes, speedometer and muffler and a clean, safe seat for the examiner, and no passengers or animals may ride along.

question.text: What skills does the road test score, and how are traffic violations treated?

answer.text: The road test scores how you prepare, control the car, enter traffic, use lanes, control speed, turn, park, back up, stop, pass and watch traffic, and you may be asked to stop on a grade; breaking a traffic law during the test is penalized.

question.text: What happens if you use a cell phone during the drive test?

answer.text: Using a cell phone during the drive test is an automatic failure, and aids such as parking assist and cruise control may not be used.

teaching.text: A phone in your hand ends the drive test at once, and assists like parking assist or cruise control stay off. Remember: phone use, instant fail.

hooks_spoken: Anyone who lives or works in Nevada and drives here needs a Nevada license, and a new resident has thirty days to apply.

hooks_spoken: New residents always take the vision test; the other tests are waived only when every condition is met.

Active-duty service members may drive on a valid home-state license.

hooks_spoken: Name and birth date are proven with one unexpired original or certified document, and a hospital birth certificate does not count.

hooks_spoken: A Real ID card shows a gold Nevada outline with a star; a standard card says it is not for Real ID purposes.
Alternative documents never support a Real ID card.

hooks_spoken: Residency takes two listed documents with a Nevada address, and a hotel or campground record needs thirty days in a row.
